title: C# Login Project · Start from Scratch
intro: Catch up on the key A Level ideas. Complete four retrieval questions, work through the examples, then practise and explain your reasoning.

questions.prompt: A rising-edge-triggered D-type flip-flop has Q = 0 and D = 1. What happens to Q when the next rising edge occurs?
questions.answer: Q becomes 1 at the rising edge because the flip-flop samples D. It then holds that value until the next triggering edge.
options: Q becomes 0 at the rising edge because the flip-flop samples D. It then holds that value until the next triggering edge.
Q becomes 1 at the rising edge because the flip-flop samples D. It then holds that value until the next triggering edge.
Q becomes 2 at the rising edge because the flip-flop samples D. It then holds that value until the next triggering edge.
questions.feedback: Model answer: Q becomes 1 at the rising edge because the flip-flop samples D. It then holds that value until the next triggering edge.

questions.prompt: Why do we group neighbouring 1s together on a Karnaugh map?
questions.answer: We group neighbouring 1s to simplify the Boolean expression. Variables that change within the group can be removed.
options: We group neighbouring 1s to simplify the Boolean expression. Variables that change within the group can be removed.
We group neighbouring 1s to simplify the Boolean expression. Variables that change within the group cannot be removed.
There is not enough information to determine the result.
questions.feedback: Model answer: We group neighbouring 1s to simplify the Boolean expression. Variables that change within the group can be removed.

questions.prompt: Push A, then B, then C onto an empty stack. Pop once and then push D. Which item is at the top, and what is the remaining stack from top to bottom?
questions.answer: D is at the top. From top to bottom the stack is D, B, A. C was removed by the pop.
options: D is not at the top. From top to bottom the stack is D, B, A. C was removed by the pop.
There is not enough information to determine the result.
D is at the top. From top to bottom the stack is D, B, A. C was removed by the pop.
questions.feedback: Model answer: D is at the top. From top to bottom the stack is D, B, A. C was removed by the pop.

questions.prompt: Using 8-bit two’s complement, write −13 and explain why simply putting 1 before the 7-bit magnitude is not correct.
questions.answer: 13 = 00001101₂. Invert to 11110010₂, then add 1: 11110011₂. Prefixing the magnitude gives sign-and-magnitude (10001101₂), not two’s complement.

blocks.title: What must a login program do?
blocks.text: Read two inputs, decide whether both match the demonstration account, and show a clear result. Design the sequence before typing code.

blocks.title: Why start with sequence?
blocks.text: Read username; read password; display what was entered only during debugging. In the final version never echo a password.

blocks.title: Introduce selection
blocks.text: Use AND (&&) to require BOTH username and password to match. One wrong value must mean access denied.

blocks.title: Make a second attempt possible
blocks.text: A loop can repeat after invalid credentials. Add a maximum number of attempts to avoid an endless loop.

blocks.title: Worked example · Model the first three lines — not the finished program
